destination.name: Bright
destination.tagline: An Ovens Valley town known for autumn colour, on the edge of the Victorian Alps.
destination.description: Bright is a town of about 2,600 people at 319 m, at the south-eastern end of the Ovens Valley in north-eastern Victoria. Tourism is its main industry, built around the autumn colours of European trees planted in the area. It is a gateway to alpine scenery near Mount Buffalo National Park, Mount Feathertop and Mount Hotham. The old rail line is now a rail trail to Wangaratta, and many paragliding launch sites lie close by.
whyVisit: See autumn colours along the river
Cycle rail trails and riverside paths

goodToKnow.title: Autumn is busiest
goodToKnow.detail: Autumn colours and the Bright Autumn Festival draw crowds, and many houses are holiday rentals. Book accommodation well ahead.

goodToKnow.title: Allow for the drive
goodToKnow.detail: It is about 3.5 hours from Melbourne by road. Public transport is limited to V/Line buses connecting at Seymour, once daily on weekends.

goodToKnow.title: River water is cold
goodToKnow.detail: Swimming in the Ovens River is popular in spring and summer, but the water is very cold, so test it before going in.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} covers autumn colour and warm summer days for swimming and rail-trail rides.
